task.title: Tolerate unrecognized refs under the shared task namespace
task.description:
A single malformed ref under refs/workbook/tasks/ on origin breaks fetch and sync for every clone until someone manually prunes it. Verified empirically at commit c453596 with a bare origin and a clone:

  git push origin HEAD:refs/workbook/tasks/EVIL

After that, `workbook sync --json` reports:
  "fetch":{"status":"failed","detail":"fetch failed before completion: task ref ID is invalid: task ID \"EVIL\" must begin with \"WB-\""}
  "push":{"status":"skipped","detail":"push skipped because fetch failed"}
and `workbook fetch --json` fails the same way. Sync was healthy immediately before the poisoning push, so the malformed ref is the sole cause.

parseOwnedRefRecords (internal/gitstore/read.go:233-267) returns an error for the entire ref listing as soon as any one name fails core.ValidateTaskID (:246). fetch (internal/gitstore/sync.go:342-357) mirrors +refs/workbook/tasks/* into the tracking namespace and then lists it, so the error aborts the whole fetch, which in turn skips the push phase (sync.go:289-294).

Anyone with push access can do this, deliberately or by accident, since refs/workbook/* is not covered by branch protection on typical hosts. A compromised or buggy agent with a push token can do it too. Local reads keep working, so the failure presents as a client bug rather than a poisoned remote, and the error text does not tell the user how to fix it.

Note the tracking namespace and the canonical namespace deserve different strictness. Refusing to write a malformed name locally is correct. Refusing to read a listing because a stranger wrote a name we do not recognize is not: it hands any collaborator a repository-wide denial of the whole sync path. listParkedRefs already tolerates stray refs and is the model to follow.

Acceptance:
- An unrecognized ref name in the tracking namespace is skipped and reported, and fetch, push, and sync complete for every well-formed task.
- The canonical namespace keeps rejecting malformed names on write.
- The report names the offending ref and states that it was ignored, so a user can prune it.
- A regression test pushes a malformed ref to a bare origin and asserts that fetch and sync still succeed for the valid tasks.
- Consider whether the same tolerance is needed for a ref whose name is valid but whose object is missing or malformed.
